Q0449

“To dare is to lose one’s footing momentarily. Not to dare is…” — Søren Kierkegaard (Either/Or)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Either/Or. Theme: courage.

Quotes / Søren Kierkegaard / Q0449

English

To dare is to lose one’s footing momentarily. Not to dare is to lose oneself.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Either/Or and files it under Existentialism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Søren Kierkegaard

Søren Kierkegaard (1813–1855) was a Danish religious author and critic of Christendom who wrote under pseudonyms exploring aesthetic, ethical, and religious existence. Inheriting a melancholy family fortune, he attacked Hegelian system and lukewarm official faith in Copenhagen.

How to read this passage

Philosophers ask whether courage is fearlessness or right action amid fear, and how it relates to recklessness, endurance, and moral courage in public life. This passage enters that discussion through courage, self, choice.

Concepts in this quote

Courage
Courage is the virtue of facing fear without abandoning judgment—central to ethics from Aristotle to modern existential resolve.
Self
Philosophy quotes about self explore identity, responsibility, and the examined life—from Socrates’ unexamined life to modern phenomenology and existential authenticity.
Choice
Choice is the hinge of agency: selecting among options under reasons, constraints, and uncertainty.
